slides.title: The Numbers Behind Every HCP Question
bullets: The p-value and 95% confidence interval are the most cited statistics in scientific communication
They are also among the most frequently misinterpreted
MSLs face technical questions about them more than almost any other topic

slides.title: The Probability of a Fluke Result
bullets: The p-value answers one narrow question: how likely is a result this extreme if there were truly no difference
By convention, a p-value below 0.05 is called statistically significant
It says nothing about the size or clinical relevance of the effect

slides.title: A Smaller P-Value Is Not a Bigger Effect
bullets: With very large samples, tiny and clinically irrelevant differences can reach statistical significance
With small samples, clinically important effects can fail to reach significance
A p-value of 0.001 only means less likely due to chance than 0.04, not a larger effect

slides.title: One Number That Does Three Jobs
bullets: The 95% confidence interval is the range expected to contain the true effect across repeated trials
It shows effect size, precision and significance together in one view
A narrower interval means a more precise estimate
If the interval doesn't cross the no-effect line, the result is statistically significant

slides.title: The Thresholds Behind Every Trial Result

stats.label: conventional p-value threshold for statistical significance
confidence level used to bound the true treatment effect

slides.caption: Methodological guidance increasingly favors the confidence interval over the p-value alone.

slides.title: Pair Every P-Value With Context
bullets: Always present the p-value alongside the 95% CI and the absolute effect size
Avoid the word demonstrated when the interval is wide or borders non-significance
Be ready to explain why statistical significance isn't automatically clinical relevance for one patient

takeaway.title: Statistical significance is not the same as clinical relevance
bullets: A p-value only tells you how unlikely a result is by chance, not how big it is
The 95% CI reveals effect size, precision and significance together
Always pair both with the absolute effect size before calling a result meaningful
